brief: Two-storey white clapboard farmhouse of the Port Oneida rural community in the gable-front-and-wing form: a tall front gable, a two-storey side wing, a small hip-roofed entrance porch on turned posts, 2/2 windows, a grey asphalt roof and a small central chimney; a marigold garden in front, a gravel drive and a weathered barn across the field.

facade.notes: the Lawr farmhouse (Port Oneida, MI, c.1900): a white two-storey gable-front-and-wing farmhouse with a porch in the angle full of potted flowers, a propane tank, a TV antenna on a pole; a log outbuilding; a mown yard cut out of the hayfield; wooded hills behind

why.note: the farmhouse yard is a mown island in the hay: the mowing is the boundary
